cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Test the Story First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to repeat the explanation, ask the dangerous question, or test the risky step before you commit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask the chair whether a bank delay could explain the missing raffle payment. Don't take my written explanation in yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell her you think that's what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No attribution during the first check, please. Find out whether the explanation holds before I attach my name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll ask which payment I mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give her the date and amount. Those are facts, not my conclusion. Come back with her answer before you volunteer mine.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assigns a test before releasing A's written explanation. A3 corrects B2's attribution and A5 distinguishes transaction facts from A's conclusion, using expert scope control to defer commitment.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 proposes naming A's belief; A3 forbids attribution in the first test. B4 asks how to identify the payment, and A5 permits factual details while withholding the conclusion.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to explain why they are asking and B4 anticipates a necessary identifying question. Both are practical concerns, not arbitrary prompts for A's method.

heightening.evidence: A5 must allow B4 enough information to make the test meaningful without volunteering A's position, tightening the same cautious strategy.

specificity.evidence: A1 raffle payment and banking-delay explanation establish the risk; A5 asks for date and amount without pretending they were already spoken aloud.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's attribution terminology is formal but directs B's actual proposal. A5's return instruction establishes when A will receive the test result.
